info.title: EODHD over Airnode
info.description:
EODHD sells end-of-day, reference and fundamental market data across some seventy exchanges. This Airnode wraps the reference, corporate action, price, news and interest rate side of it: what instruments exist and how they are identified, what has been paid out on them, what they closed at, what is being written about them, and what central banks and the US Treasury have set.

Much of it is settled. A paid dividend, a completed split, a closed session, a past policy rate and a published Treasury curve all stop changing, so two Airnodes asked afterwards agree and their attestations aggregate. The quotes, the news and the sentiment do not: those move, and an attestation over one is provenance for the instant it was taken.

EODHD's fundamentals product, which is the company profile, the financial statements, the earnings and the ownership, is sold separately and is not among the operations this Airnode serves.

Every response carries an EIP-191 signature from the Airnode that served it, so the data can be attributed back to its source rather than trusted on reputation.

get.description: Describes the operations this Airnode serves and how to verify what it returns. Free.

200.description: An OpenAPI document describing this Airnode.

post.summary: Perform an operation and attest to the response.

oneOf.title: searchInstruments
oneOf.description: Turn a company name, a partial ticker, or an ISIN, CUSIP, FIGI, LEI or SEC CIK into the EODHD tickers the other operations take.

operation.description:
The way in. Nothing else here accepts a name, and a ticker has to be spelled SYMBOL.EXCHANGE exactly, so an intent that starts from a company rather than from a ticker starts here. Names, tickers and every identifier share one index: searching an ISIN returns the primary listing and every cross-listing of it, thirteen of them for Apple.

A query that matches nothing answers with an empty array rather than an error, which is the one case worth checking for before reading a result. identifierMapping goes the other way, from a ticker to those identifiers.

query.description: A company name, a symbol or a fragment of either, or an ISIN, CUSIP, FIGI, LEI or SEC CIK, the CIK with or without its leading zeros. Matching is loose and unanchored, so apple returns AAPL.US alongside a crypto pair whose symbol contains it.

type.description: Narrow to one kind of instrument. These are not the spellings that come back under Type, so a caller filtering and then matching on the response needs both: stock returns Common Stock, etf returns ETF, fund returns FUND, bond returns BOND, index returns INDEX, and crypto returns Currency.

exchange.description: Narrow to one exchange, by the code exchangeList returns. Without it the answer spans every exchange EODHD covers, which is why a name search returns the same company many times over. It also includes listings on exchanges exchangeList leaves out, such as NSE and TA, which every other operation answers 404 for.

bonds_only.description: Return bonds and nothing else, which is what type=bond already does: the two answered identically on every query tried. An integer rather than a boolean because EODHD reads the value the way PHP does, so the string a boolean would send is not the falsy spelling.

responseProjection.description: Optional. Maps a name of your choosing to an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response, such as {"price": "/ethereum/usd"}. data is then the text of a JSON object of those names in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it, instead of the whole body, and the projection is part of the signed request identity. No two names take the same pointer, and no pointer is inside another's value. A pointer the response does not have is a 400.

oneOf.title: exchangeList
oneOf.description: The exchanges the other operations serve, with the code that spells the half of a ticker after the dot.

operation.description:
Seventy exchanges, and the only place their codes are enumerated. INDX, for indices, is served without being listed. searchInstruments also returns listings on exchanges this leaves out, such as NSE and TA, which no other operation serves. Worth one call before a run of searches, since it is what makes the exchange filter on searchInstruments usable and what tells an EODHD code apart from the MICs it covers.

Takes no parameters, so the answer is the same for every caller and changes only when EODHD adds an exchange.

oneOf.title: identifierMapping
oneOf.description: Every other identifier EODHD holds for a ticker: ISIN, FIGI, LEI, CUSIP and the SEC filer number.

operation.description:
What searchInstruments does not carry. A search answers with names and prices; this answers with the identifiers a custodian, a regulator or a filing would use for the same listing, which is what a consumer reconciling against one of those needs.

EODHD requires at least one of filter[symbol], filter[isin], filter[figi], filter[lei], filter[cusip] and filter[cik], and refuses a call carrying none with a 422. OpenAPI cannot say one-of, so this declares the ticker one and requires it. A caller holding an ISIN instead uses searchInstruments, which matches ISINs too and answers with every listing of the instrument.

filter[symbol].description: An EODHD ticker, spelled SYMBOL.EXCHANGE. Matches the one listing.

oneOf.title: stockScreener
oneOf.description: Listings across every exchange that match filters on price, size, returns, volume, sector and dividends.

operation.description:
Reaches the first 1,000 matches and no further: offset and limit together stop there. Without sort the order is arbitrary.

market_capitalization is in each listing's own currency, but sorting on it orders by a common one, so 175 trillion THB for NVDA80 on BK sorts beside 5.2 trillion USD. A filter, signal or field EODHD does not know is a 422, which reaches a caller as a 502. Each call is metered as 5.

filters.description: A JSON array of [field, operation, value] conditions, such as [["market_capitalization",">",1000000000000],["exchange","=","us"]]. The fields are code, name, exchange, sector, industry, market_capitalization, earnings_share, dividend_yield, refund_1d_p, refund_5d_p, avgvol_1d, avgvol_200d and adjusted_close. Operations include =, > and match. A field, operation or signal EODHD does not know is a 422, which reaches a caller as a 502.

signals.description: Precomputed flags, comma separated: 200d_new_lo, 200d_new_hi, bookvalue_neg, bookvalue_pos, wallstreet_lo and wallstreet_hi.

sort.description: A filter field and a direction, asc or desc. Without it the order is arbitrary. market_capitalization is in each listing's own currency, but sorting orders by a common one, so 175 trillion THB sorts beside 5.2 trillion USD.

offset.description: Rows to skip. offset and limit together reach the first 1,000 matches and no further.

responseProjection.description: Optional. oneOf.title: dividendHistory
oneOf.description: Every dividend a listing has paid, with its declaration, record and payment dates and both the adjusted and declared value.

operation.description:
Settled data, which is the half of this API worth aggregating across Airnodes: once a dividend is paid the record stops changing, so two Airnodes asked afterwards agree. Apple returns 92 payments back to 1987.

value is adjusted for every split since and unadjustedValue is what was declared, so the two differ on any payment made before a split and agree on one made after. splitHistory is what explains the difference. An instrument that has never paid a dividend answers with an empty array, and so does a crypto or currency pair.

ticker.description: The listing, spelled SYMBOL.EXCHANGE: AAPL.US, VOD.LSE, BMW.XETRA. The exchange half is EODHD's own code rather than a MIC, and a bare symbol is refused. A ticker EODHD does not hold answers 404, which reaches a caller as a 502 rather than as an empty answer. searchInstruments is where one comes from.

from.description: Earliest ex-dividend date to return. Omitted, the answer starts at the first payment on record.

to.description: Latest ex-dividend date to return. Omitted, the answer runs to the most recent payment.

responseProjection.description: Optional. oneOf.description: Every stock split a listing has had, which is what makes an old price or dividend comparable to a current one.

operation.description: Settled data, like dividendHistory, and the reason its value and unadjustedValue differ: a split is what an adjustment adjusts for. Each split is a new-over-old ratio. Apple returns five since 1987, the most recent being 4:1 in August 2020. An instrument that has never split answers with an empty array.

oneOf.title: eodPrices
oneOf.description: Settled daily, weekly or monthly bars for one listing, with the split-adjusted close alongside the traded one.

operation.description:
The end of day series, which is settled: once a session closes the bar stops changing, so two Airnodes asked afterwards agree. That is what separates it from delayedQuote beside it, which moves all day.

adjusted_close is corrected for every split and dividend since and close is what actually traded, so a series compared across a split has to use the first. Narrow with from and to, which work here unlike on the Treasury operations.

ticker.description: The listing, spelled SYMBOL.EXCHANGE: AAPL.US, VOD.LSE, BMW.XETRA. The exchange half is EODHD's own code rather than a MIC, and a bare symbol is refused. A ticker EODHD does not hold answers 404, which reaches a caller as a 502 rather than as an empty answer. searchInstruments is where one comes from. Crypto and currency pairs are spelled the same way: BTC-USD.CC, EURUSD.FOREX.

from.description: Earliest session to return. Omitted, the answer reaches as far back as the plan allows.

to.description: Latest session to return. Omitted, the answer runs to the last settled session.

period.description: Group the bars. Weekly and monthly bars are built from the daily ones and dated to the start of the period.

responseProjection.description: Optional. oneOf.title: intradayPrices
oneOf.description: Intraday bars for one listing, from one minute to one hour.

operation.description:
Times are in UTC. 5m and 1h cover the regular session only. 1m, 15m and 30m add pre-market and after-hours bars: for US listings they run from 08:00 to midnight UTC.

One range may span at most 120 days at 1m and 600 days at 5m. A longer one is a 422 from EODHD, which reaches a caller as a 502. Without from and to the answer is the last 120 days, which at 1m is 80,000 bars and 11 MB. Each call is metered as 5.

ticker.description: The listing, spelled SYMBOL.EXCHANGE: AAPL.US, VOD.LSE, BMW.XETRA. The exchange half is EODHD's own code rather than a MIC, and a bare symbol is refused. A ticker EODHD does not hold answers 404, which reaches a caller as a 502 rather than as an empty answer. searchInstruments is where one comes from. Crypto and currency pairs are spelled the same way: BTC-USD.CC, EURUSD.FOREX.

interval.description: Bar length. 5m and 1h cover the regular session only, and 1m, 15m and 30m add pre-market and after-hours bars.

from.description: Start, in Unix seconds. Without from and to, the last 120 days. A range over 120 days at 1m or 600 days at 5m is refused.

oneOf.title: technicalIndicator
oneOf.description: A technical indicator computed over a listing's daily series, one value per session.

operation.description:
from bounds the input as well as the output, so the first value comes period sessions after it: an sma with period 14 over a five-day window is []. Without from and to, the series runs from the listing's first session, which for AAPL.US is 11,510 rows.

The fields of each row depend on function. Each call is metered as 5.

ticker.description: The listing, spelled SYMBOL.EXCHANGE: AAPL.US, VOD.LSE, BMW.XETRA. The exchange half is EODHD's own code rather than a MIC, and a bare symbol is refused. A ticker EODHD does not hold answers 404, which reaches a caller as a 502 rather than as an empty answer. searchInstruments is where one comes from. Crypto and currency pairs are spelled the same way: BTC-USD.CC, EURUSD.FOREX.

function.description: What to compute. splitadjusted returns split-adjusted daily bars rather than an indicator.

period.description: Sessions per value. stochastic, macd and sar ignore it and take their own periods below.

from.description: First session of input, not of output: the first value comes period sessions later, so a window shorter than period is []. Omitted, the input starts at the listing's first session.

order.description: a for oldest first, d for newest first.

splitadjusted_only.description: 1 adjusts the input for splits but not for dividends.

agg_period.description: Bar length for splitadjusted. Other functions ignore it.

oneOf.title: delayedQuote
oneOf.description: A delayed quote for one listing, or for several at once, with the day so far and the change on the previous close.

operation.description:
Delayed rather than live, by whatever the exchange requires, so an attestation over one is provenance for that instant and two Airnodes asked a second apart will disagree. eodPrices is the settled counterpart.

**The shape depends on how many tickers were asked for.** One is an object; adding any through s makes it an array, including when only one more is added. Both are declared, and a consumer has to handle each.

Before the session opens, open is 0 rather than null.

ticker.description: The listing, spelled SYMBOL.EXCHANGE: AAPL.US, VOD.LSE, BMW.XETRA. The exchange half is EODHD's own code rather than a MIC, and a bare symbol is refused. A ticker EODHD does not hold answers 200 with NA in every figure rather than an error. searchInstruments is where one comes from. Crypto and currency pairs are spelled the same way: BTC-USD.CC, EURUSD.FOREX. Before the session opens, open is 0.

s.description: Further tickers, comma separated. Supplying any turns the answer from one object into an array, the ticker in the path included, so read code on each row rather than assuming an order. A ticker EODHD does not hold comes back as a row of NA.

responseProjection.description: Optional. oneOf.title: usDelayedQuotes
oneOf.description: Delayed US quotes with the reference and valuation figures attached: market cap, P/E, sector, float and dividend yield.

operation.description:
Richer than delayedQuote and US listings only. It carries the bid and ask with their sizes and times, the moving averages, the 52-week range, and a block of company reference data that is otherwise part of the fundamentals product: marketCap, pe, forwardPE, sector, industry, sharesFloat, sharesOutstanding, dividendYield and payoutRatio. That makes it the only operation here that answers a valuation question at all.

EODHD documents the parameter as symbols. It is s, and the documented spelling is refused with a 422.

A ticker it does not quote is left out of data rather than refused, so count can come back lower than asked, as it did with TCEHY.US among five.

s.description: One or more US tickers, comma separated, as in AAPL.US,MSFT.US. Required, and named s rather than the symbols their document declares. A ticker it does not quote is left out of data rather than refused, and data is [] when none is.

fields.description: Return only the named fields, comma separated, rather than the whole quote.

responseProjection.description: Optional. oneOf.title: news
oneOf.description: Financial news articles for a ticker or a tag, with each article carrying its own sentiment scores.

operation.description:
The articles themselves, body included, which is what makes this the heaviest news operation: two articles are 8 KB. A caller wanting only the mood over time should ask newsSentiment instead and never pay for the text.

Moves continuously, so an attestation over it is provenance for the instant rather than something two Airnodes will agree on.

s.description: A ticker, spelled SYMBOL.EXCHANGE. One of s or t is needed for a useful answer.

t.description: A tag to filter by instead of a ticker, such as a topic EODHD classifies articles under.

from.description: Earliest publication date to return. Omitted, the answer starts at the oldest article held.

to.description: Latest publication date to return. Omitted, the answer runs to the newest.

limit.description: Articles to return. Each carries its full body, so this is what bounds the payload.

offset.description: Articles to skip, for walking further back.

responseProjection.description: Optional. oneOf.title: newsSentiment
oneOf.description: Daily aggregated news sentiment per ticker, as a score and the article count behind it, without the article text.

operation.description:
The cheap counterpart to news: the same underlying articles reduced to one number a day, so a year of mood costs a kilobyte rather than megabytes. Read count alongside normalized, since a strong score resting on one article says less than a middling one resting on sixty.

Takes several tickers at once and keys the answer by ticker.

s.description: One or more tickers, comma separated, as in AAPL.US,BTC-USD.CC. A ticker EODHD does not hold answers [] rather than an object.

from.description: Earliest date to return. Omitted, the answer starts at the oldest day held.

to.description: Latest date to return. Omitted, the answer runs to today.

oneOf.title: newsWordWeights
oneOf.description: The words carrying most weight in recent coverage of a ticker.

operation.description:
What the coverage is actually about, rather than how positive it is. Useful for telling two identical sentiment scores apart: the same score over earnings coverage and over litigation coverage mean different things.

The payload is a free-form word-to-weight map, so the keys are the words themselves and vary with every call.

filter[date_to].description: Latest publication date to draw words from.

oneOf.title: treasuryYieldCurve
oneOf.description: The US Treasury constant maturity yield curve, every tenor for every trading day of the year so far.

operation.description:
The official curve, from Treasury rather than from a broker, and the series most other rates are read against. Settled and heavily used, which makes it one of the better things here to attest.

One row per tenor per day, 2,282 of them and 108 KB at the time of writing, growing through the year.

**Takes no parameters.** EODHD declares from, to, filter[year], page[limit] and page[offset] on this endpoint and ignores every one of them: each spelling returns the identical full series. None is declared here, because a parameter an Airnode accepts and hashes and that changes nothing is an attestation naming a request that was never really made.

oneOf.description: US Treasury bill auction rates, discount and coupon equivalent, with the CUSIP and maturity of each bill.

operation.description:
The short end, quoted the way bills are: a discount rate and its coupon equivalent, plus the auction averages. The CUSIP and maturity date make each row a specific bill rather than a point on a curve, which is what separates this from treasuryYieldCurve.

1,141 rows and 175 KB at the time of writing, the largest of the four.

**Takes no parameters.** EODHD declares from, to, filter[year], page[limit] and page[offset] on this endpoint and ignores every one of them: each spelling returns the identical full series. oneOf.title: treasuryLongTermRates
oneOf.description: The US Treasury long-term composite rates.

operation.description:
The extrapolated long end, which is what Treasury publishes where no on-the-run issue exists at that maturity. Rows carry a rate_type such as BC_20year or LT_COMPOSITE rather than the plain tenor treasuryYieldCurve uses, so the two do not join on tenor.

489 rows and 43 KB at the time of writing.

**Takes no parameters.** EODHD declares from, to, filter[year], page[limit] and page[offset] on this endpoint and ignores every one of them: each spelling returns the identical full series. None is declared here, because a parameter an Airnode accepts and hashes and that changes nothing is an attestation naming a request that was never really made.

responseProjection.description: Optional. Maps a name of your choosing to an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response, such as {"price": "/ethereum/usd"}. data is then the text of a JSON object of those names in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it, instead of the whole body, and the projection is part of the signed request identity. No two names take the same pointer, and no pointer is inside another's value. A pointer the response does not have is a 400.

oneOf.title: treasuryRealYields
oneOf.description: US Treasury real yield curve rates, which are the inflation-indexed counterpart to the nominal curve.

operation.description:
What TIPS yield, tenor by tenor. Subtracting these from treasuryYieldCurve at the same tenor is how a breakeven inflation rate is taken, which is the main reason to want both.

815 rows and 39 KB at the time of writing, and the same shape as treasuryYieldCurve.

**Takes no parameters.** EODHD declares from, to, filter[year], page[limit] and page[offset] on this endpoint and ignores every one of them: each spelling returns the identical full series. None is declared here, because a parameter an Airnode accepts and hashes and that changes nothing is an attestation naming a request that was never really made.

oneOf.title: commodityPrices
oneOf.description: Commodity price history: oil, natural gas, metals, grains, softs, uranium and an all-commodities index.

operation.description:
Newest first. WTI reaches back to 1986, most others to 1992. Each call is metered as 5.

from and to are ignored, so a window comes from paging. EODHD lists GOLD, SILVER, COFFEE and eleven more codes besides these, and every one of them answers 404.

code.description: The series. ALL_COMMODITIES is an index, 2016 = 100. GOLD, SILVER and the other codes EODHD lists besides these answer 404.

interval.description: Period of each value. daily and weekly exist only for WTI, BRENT and NATURAL_GAS, and are a 422 elsewhere.

responseProjection.description: Optional. Maps a name of your choosing to an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response, such as {"price": "/ethereum/usd"}. data is then the text of a JSON object of those names in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it, instead of the whole body, and the projection is part of the signed request identity. No two names take the same pointer, and no pointer is inside another's value. A pointer the response does not have is a 400.

200.description: The upstream response and the attestation over it.

400.description: The operation exists but the parameters or the projection are missing, unknown or malformed, a path parameter is empty, . or .. or has such a part between slashes, or the projection names too many fields, an empty or repeated pointer, or a path the response does not have. Also a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header that does not decode to a payment payload.

402.description: The operation is paid and no valid payment was supplied. The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header carries the x402 payment requirements to retry against.

502.description: The upstream API could not be reached or refused the request.

airnode.description: The address whose signature attests to this response.

requestHash.description: Identifies the request this response answers.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds at which the response was signed.

data.description: The upstream response body exactly as received, less a leading byte order mark. With a projection, the text of a JSON object keyed by the names it asked for in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it.

attestation.digest: keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes32 requestHash, uint256 timestamp, bytes dataBytes))
attestation.requestHash: keccak256(utf8(JSON.stringify([operation, parameterEntriesSortedByName]))), where an object value is itself entries sorted by name, at any depth, and an array keeps its order. Names are compared by Unicode code point. A request that carries a projection appends its entries, sorted the same way, as a third element
attestation.verify: Recover the signer of the signature over the digest and check it equals the address above.

parameters.x-airnode-sign: false skips the signature: no attestation headers, and the body streamed through with no size cap.
parameters.x-airnode-project: alias:pointer, once per field to keep and at most 20 times, each pointer an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response that starts with /, is not repeated and is not inside another's value. The body becomes an object of those aliases in Unicode code point order, the signature covers it, and a pointer the response does not have is a 400.

passthrough.flow: Send the request the provider documents, method, path, query and body as they are, to url followed by the route's path. The body comes back as the upstream sent it, with the upstream's status, and on success the attestation is in the X-Airnode-Address, X-Airnode-Request-Hash, X-Airnode-Timestamp and X-Airnode-Signature headers, with the operation served in X-Airnode-Operation. Every query parameter starting with x-airnode- is this Airnode's own, listed under parameters, and never reaches the upstream.
passthrough.requestHash: keccak256(utf8(JSON.stringify(["passthrough", method, path, queryEntries, headerEntries, body]))), where method is upper case, path is what was sent after url as a URL parser resolves it, the query entries are what was sent with the Airnode's own parameters removed, in the order sent, headerEntries are the headers that the routes declare as parameters and the request sent, each name in lower case and sorted by Unicode code point, with the values of a header sent more than once joined with ", " in the order sent and the result trimmed of spaces and tabs, and body is the request body as sent, or an empty string. A request that carries a projection appends its entries, sorted by name in Unicode code point order, as a seventh element
passthrough.dataBytes: UTF-8 of the response body exactly as received, less a leading byte order mark, or of the projected object

payment.flow: An unpaid call to a priced operation returns 402 with the x402 payment requirements, base64-encoded, in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header. Sign an EIP-3009 authorization matching one entry and retry the call with the payment payload, base64-encoded, in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. The settlement receipt comes back in the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header.
